glosses: To plan, control and record the position and course of a vehicle, ship, aircraft, etc., on a journey; to follow a planned course.

examples.text: He navigated the bomber to the Ruhr.

Earlier this month, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration began an investigation into four crashes of Teslas operating with a partial-automation system (which can navigate highways and steer the car on city streets but requires a licensed driver to be present), including one in which a pedestrian was killed. In a news release, NHTSA said reduced visibility may have led to the crashes.

examples.text: You drive. I'll navigate.

glosses: To travel over water in a ship; to sail.

examples.text: We navigated to France in the dinghy.

glosses: To move between web pages, menus, etc. by means of hyperlinks, mouse clicks, or any other mechanism.

examples.text: It was difficult to navigate back to the home page.

glosses: To find a way through a difficult situation or process.

examples.text: However, given current sensibilities about individual privacy and data protection, the recording of oral data is becoming increasingly onerous for researchers who are obliged to navigate an often time-consuming and complex series of administrative requirements and corollary review processes in order to be granted ethics clearance.
